title: Targeted Counterfactual Branch Augmentation for Robust Text-Based World Models under Agent Policy Shift

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to improve text-based world model robustness under agent policy shift without expensive multi-agent trajectory collection.  
- **Paper [1]** discusses the role of world models in improving learning efficiency for agents in text-based environments but does not explicitly address robustness under policy shift or avoiding multi-agent trajectory collection.  
- **Paper [2]** focuses on pre-trained language models as a base for world models in text-based games but does not address robustness under policy shift or the specific cost-saving aspect.  
- **Paper [10]** explores whether language models can serve as text-based world simulators but does not target robustness under policy shift or cost reduction.  
- **Paper [15]** addresses robustness to distribution shifts but does not focus on text-based world models or the specific cost-saving aspect.  
No prior paper explicitly shares the same objective at the problem-class level.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves Targeted Counterfactual Branch Augmentation (TCBA), which generates counterfactual branches weighted by the out-of-distribution (OOD) agent's action distribution, using targeting weights computed from OOD agent calibration runs.  
- **Paper [4]** introduces counterfactual augmentation for correcting presentation bias but does not involve weighting branches by OOD agent action distributions or calibration runs.  
- **Paper [5]** discusses counterfactual world models but focuses on video diffusion and digital twin conditioning, not targeted counterfactual branching based on OOD agent calibration.  
- **Paper [6]** and **Paper [7]** explore counterfactual data augmentation for OOD robustness but do not involve targeted branching or calibration-based weighting.  
- **Paper [11]** introduces ACAMDA, which uses causal modeling for counterfactual estimation but does not involve targeted branching or OOD agent calibration.  
No prior paper employs the same mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring consistency ratio improvements on ScienceWorld, comparing TCBA against random branching and expert-only training.  
- **Paper [1]** uses text-based environments for studying world models but does not use ScienceWorld or consistency ratio metrics.  
- **Paper [10]** introduces ByteSized32-State-Prediction as a benchmark for text-based world simulators but does not use ScienceWorld or consistency ratio metrics.  
- **Paper [15]** compares methods for robustness to distribution shifts but does not use ScienceWorld or consistency ratio metrics.  
No prior paper uses the same evaluation design.

### Domain
The domain is text-based world models.  
- **Paper [1]** explicitly studies text-based world models.  
- **Paper [2]** focuses on PLM-based world models for text-based games.  
- **Paper [10]** explores language models as text-based world simulators.  
The domain is covered by prior work.
